from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Introduction: The Chaos of the Coffee Cup", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Assuming asset path is correct and files exist locally in provided environment
        coffee = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/coffee.svg")

        self.place_at_grid(coffee, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(cream, 'B1', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(coffee), FadeIn(cream))
        self.play(cream.animate.move_to(coffee.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Rotate(cream, angle=PI*2, about_point=coffee.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(RED)
        re_label = Text("Re", font_size=36, color=RED)
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=RED)
        
        self.place_at_grid(re_label, 'E2')
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'E4')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(re_label), GrowArrow(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Kolmogorov Cascade: Energy Transfer", [
            "Large eddies break down into smaller energy-containing ones.",
            "Energy cascades down to the smallest viscous scales.",
            "The energy spectrum follows a minus five-thirds law."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Draw large circles representing eddies that split into smaller ones
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        eddy_asset = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/whirlpool.svg"
        large_eddy = SVGMobject(eddy_asset).set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(large_eddy, 'B3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(large_eddy))
        
        small_eddies = VGroup(*[SVGMobject(eddy_asset).set_color(TEAL) for _ in range(4)])
        self.place_at_grid(small_eddies[0], 'D2', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(small_eddies[1], 'D3', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(small_eddies[2], 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(small_eddies[3], 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(large_eddy, small_eddies), run_time=2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        energy_arrows = VGroup(*[Arrow(start=large_eddy.get_center(), end=e.get_center(), buff=0.1, color=ORANGE) for e in small_eddies])
        self.play(Create(energy_arrows))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 6], y_range=[0, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'F3', scale_factor=0.8)
        graph = axes.plot(lambda x: x**(-5/3) * 5, x_range=[1, 5], color=RED)

        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Real-World Application", [
            "Constants help predict drag without solving every vortex.",
            "Reynolds number, spectra, and scale define turbulence regimes.",
            "These models improve efficiency in engineering real-world designs."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display an airplane wing [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/airplane.svg] with smooth predicted drag lines.
        airplane = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/airplane.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(airplane, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        drag_line = Line(start=LEFT*1, end=RIGHT*1, color=BLUE).next_to(airplane, UP)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(airplane), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Create(drag_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Flash summary terms: 'Re', 'Spectra', 'Scale' in white (#FFFFFF).
        terms = VGroup(
            Text("Re", color=WHITE),
            Text("Spectra", color=WHITE),
            Text("Scale", color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5).scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(terms, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(terms))
        self.play(terms.animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Transition to an engineering blueprint of a turbine [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/turbine.svg].
        turbine = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/turbine.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(turbine, 'B2', scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(airplane), FadeOut(drag_line), FadeOut(terms),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN)
        )
        self.play(FadeIn(turbine))
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Introduction: The Chaos of the Coffee Cup
sections.content: Briefly introduce the phenomenon of turbulence using the analogy of cream swirling in a cup of coffee. Define turbulence as non-linear, multi-scale motion and establish the Reynolds number (Re) as the prerequisite non-dimensional parameter that dictates transition to chaos.
sections.example: Visualizing cream eddies: A small stir (low Re) leads to smooth streamlines; a rapid stir (high Re) creates a hierarchy of swirling structures.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Cascade: Energy Transfer
sections.content: Explain Richardson’s cascade: large eddies break into smaller ones, transferring kinetic energy down to the viscous scale. Introduce the energy spectrum E(k) ~ k^(-5/3) as the 'DNA' of turbulence.
sections.example: An animated 'Russian Nesting Doll' model where large vortices (parent) spawn smaller, faster-spinning vortices (children) until friction dissipates the energy.

sections.title: The Kolmogorov Constant (C): A Universal Signature
sections.content: Introduce Kolmogorov’s hypothesis of local isotropy. The constant 'C' (~1.5) appears in the spectrum formula: E(k) = C * ε^(2/3) * k^(-5/3). Emphasize that this constant is universal, regardless of the fluid.
sections.example: A comparison animation: Turbulence in a mountain stream vs. turbulence in the atmosphere of Jupiter, both collapsing onto the same -5/3 slope graph.

sections.title: Mathematical Structure: The Dissipation Scale
sections.content: Define the Kolmogorov length scale η (eta). This is the 'mathematical cliff' where viscosity dominates and kinetic energy is converted to heat, ending the mathematical structure of the cascade.
sections.example: An animation of a 'Tornado' character shrinking down; at the macro-scale, it's a storm, but as it reaches scale η, it flattens and vanishes into a 'thermal glow'.

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Application
sections.content: Synthesize how these constants allow engineers to predict drag and mixing without solving every tiny vortex. Recap: Re defines the regime, k^(-5/3) defines the structure, and η defines the limit.
sections.example: Designing an aircraft wing: Using the -5/3 law to estimate how the 'turbulent noise' around the wing affects fuel efficiency.
